# Shared memory (your own settings beat the project's here: a vault path is personal)
memory.backend = files    (default)
memory.dir = <ROOT>/.council/memory    (default)

# Council Loop settings. Every key is optional: delete what you do not need.
#
# Two files, same shape:
#   <project>/.council/config.yaml    for one project (commit it)
#   ~/.council/config.yaml            your own defaults on this machine
# Who wins: a command-line flag, then the project's file, then your own file, then the defaults
# shown here. One exception: for `memory:` your own file wins, because a vault path is personal, and
# a project's file may only name a folder inside the project. Two sections at the end belong to one
# file only.
# See what is in force, and who set it:  council config

members:
  research:                  # shorthand: `research: 3` (how many) or `research: false` (none)
    seats: 2                 # 0 to 4 researchers. Flag: --research N, --no-research
    budget:                  # searches or page reads per researcher. Flag: --research-budget N
      lite: 10
      full: 15
    later_loops: on_request  # research again before loops 2 and 3: on_request (a member asked) | always | never
    model: auto              # auto: models that can search the web, from different labs | chair: the strongest model
    # beats:                 # replace the built-in beats (papers; practice; the case against; the project's own record)
    #   - name: Regulation
    #     text: Laws, regulator guidance and enforcement actions that apply to this decision, by jurisdiction.

  map:                       # shorthand: `map: always` | `map: never`
    when: stale              # stale: only when the map is missing or behind the code | always | never. Flag: --map, --no-map
    path: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md   # where the map lives (default: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md if docs/ exists, else ARCHITECTURE.md)
    model: chair             # chair: the strongest model writes the map | expert: an expert-seat model (cheaper)
    skeleton_lines: 420      # length of the script-made skeleton the mapper reads
    focus_tokens: 700        # size of the ranked code list packets carry when the ask names code; 0 = none. Flag: --focus-tokens N

  digest: 14                 # how many facts from the shared memory each packet carries (0 to 40)

memory:                      # set with: council memory setup --obsidian --vault "<path>"   (or --files)
  backend: files             # files | obsidian
  # dir: .council/memory     # for files
  # vault: /path/to/your/vault         # for obsidian (put this in YOUR file, not the project's)
  # folder: Council Loop/<project>     # folder inside the vault

# --- the project's file only -------------------------------------------------------------------
# tripwires:                 # a name and a pattern: an ask that matches is raised to the Full tier
#   billing: "\\bbilling\\b|\\binvoices?\\b"       # letter case is ignored; no look-around, no back-references, 200 characters at most
# tripwire_paths:            # a name and globs: touching such a file (--paths) raises the tier too
#   billing: ["billing/*", "*/ledger/*"]

# --- your own file only (~/.council/config.yaml) ------------------------------------------------
# A project's file cannot set these: what a run costs and what a server offers are yours to decide.
# defaults:
#   profile: efficient       # efficient (the default, cheapest) | balanced | max
#   mode: fanout:claude      # default: the cheapest mode this machine can reach (council doctor shows it)
# mcp:                       # the MCP server (council mcp); a flag or a COUNCIL_MCP_* variable beats these
#   project: /path/to/project   # serve this one project and refuse others
#   read_only: false         # true: offer only the operations that change nothing
#   dispatch: true           # false: never offer an operation that sends prompts to model vendors
#   toolsets: [run, memory, map]   # groups of tools: run, memory, map, blocks, or all
#   deny_tools: []           # operations never to offer, e.g. [memory_setup]
#   output_schemas: false    # true: list every tool's output schema too (a larger tool list)
